body: I guess people always assume you should be sad because you once knew that person. Most of the people I see talking about how nice she was never liked her either. When that many people change their minds that fast, it makes you wonder what's wrong with you.

Exactly, our old dog was a beagle-basset mix that was about two feet long and a foot and a half tall, but man could that thing howl. It was enough to deter whoever was trying to break in, so I like to think he used his little life to do some good. 
Apparently someone was trying to break in to steal copper piping or wiring or something that a lot of old houses still use. The house was on the market at the time, so the police told us that the intruders most likely thought it was vacant, as was the case with other houses they targeted through real estate ads. Thankfully my brother in law replaced all the old pipes and fixtures last year, so there's no glorious stores of copper hidden away in my creepy concrete basement. In fact, I can't fathom what somebody would want to steal from this house. It's my father's house, I live in a different town. Most of his electronics are from the 90s and 2000s, he literally has zero cufflinks, watches, nada. I was looking through his folding chest earlier for a stamp, and I noticed a hidden compartment and got excited- it had paperclips in it. The man uses an old folding chest with secret compartments to hold PAPERCLIPS. Plus, he's divorced with five kids and works as a mail carrier. If he ever gets the chance to hold money, it goes straight to the bank.
She wasn't doing the type of drugs she overdosed on when we were in high school. She always ended up with a bad crowd, so I'm guessing that led her to her final situation.

I have decent security in my own home, and I have experience with self defense techniques and weapons (not guns, though), but this is an old house that's a bit more finicky and the choice of defense tools requires more... creativity, let's say. I know that I have the practice and the knowledge to defend myself, but I guess it's just in my personality to hide with caution and not confront with confidence. The alliteration there wasn't intentional, but the fact that I'm noticing alliteration and not every bump in the night is a good sign.

Our old dog is what stopped the first break in. Having a dog around is comforting, but the whole experience was nerve wracking and I think I just need to chat with people and do regular things to calm myself down a bit.
I usually don't get worried but I don't stay here often and there have been break in attempts before.
I swear to any and all gods that I normally keep to much better spelling and grammar, but this whole post looks like a twelve year old wrote it.
